correctness.rationale: The longitudinal fibers in the square are chains in the primitive direction (q,-p). The longest has h+1 entries, h=floor(2N/s): its end-to-end maximum coordinate displacement is hs, and any such integer segment fits by separate coordinate translations. Each loop gives at most one Fourier coefficient on that fiber, so fewer than h+1 loops cannot give injectivity at any offsets. Bezout transverse coordinates give distinct equally spaced offsets whose root sum kills every nonzero alias step |r|<=h when L>=h+1. This proves Parseval with the given Haar and arclength probability normalization. The least feasible integer s is s_L=1+floor(2N/L). For s_L>=2, primitiveness forces the other coordinate nonzero and the minimum squared winding is s_L^2+1, with equality precisely for signed coordinate permutations of (s_L,1). When s_L=1 the unit axes attain the minimum. For L<=2N, Ls_L>=2N+1 and the length is strictly larger than 2pi(2N+1); otherwise it is 2pi L, uniquely minimized at L=2N+1. The checker was inspected, not executed; its 12,544 alias cases are corroboration, not the proof.
residual_risks: The proof is for distinct parallel complete primitive loops with equal probabilities and excludes transit between loops and arbitrary mixed-direction or curved designs.

evidence: Before imposing exactness, the displayed (T_v+1)-square moment block already factors into L outer products. It is the Gram block of a full chain of T_v+1 frequencies separated by (q,-p); such a chain fits in the square because T_v max(|p|,|q|)<=2N.
If L<T_v+1, the block is singular for every offset, which yields noninjectivity, not only failure of exactness. Conversely the moment criterion yields exactness from regular L-gon offsets when L>T_v.

Solving L>T_v for s gives s>=1+floor(2N/L); the shortest primitive vector above that integer floor is a coordinate direction if the floor expression is 1, and otherwise a signed permutation of (s_L,1).
